This is a petition seeking setting aside of the impugned order dated 17.01.2023 passed by learned ASJ, South West District, Dwarka Courts titled 'State vs. Jai Kishore Kumar' wherein charges have been framed against the petitioner u/s 427/506/509/354D/354 IPC and Sections 6 read with 5(1) of POCSO Act and in the alternative Section 376(2)(n) IPC.
It is stated by Mr. Tiwari, learned counsel for the petitioner that the Sessions Court has not sifted and weighed the material before the Court while framing the charges.

sentences.text: It is clarified that it is not compulsory for the prosecutrix to appear in person for the hearing.

This is an application seeking stay in FIR No. 413/2022 u/s 323/427/506/509/354/354D/376(2)(n)
IPC and Sections 6 read with 5(1) of POCSO Act and in the alternative Section 376(2)(n) IPC.
In the present case, prima facie, even assuming the statement u/s 164 Cr.P.C. to be correct, the prosecutrix was in a relationship with the petitioner.
Even as per statement u/s 164 Cr.P.C., the respondent has stated that she was in a relationship with the petitioner since 2012.
However, there This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 14:06:06 is no explanation as to why no steps were taken by the respondent for registering the FIR earlier.
My attention has also been drawn to a letter written to the SHO, PS Tilak Nagar as late as 31.08.2021, wherein there is no such allegation against the petitioner.
In fact, the same is an apology letter for creating nuisance at the office of the petitioner.
Even in the FIR dated 27.05.2022, there are no allegation of sexual assault against the petitioner.

The first time the allegations have been made are only in the statement u/s 164 Cr.P.C.
I am of the view that the matter needs consideration.

Prima facie, if the prosecutrix was sexually assaulted by blackmail and by threats, there is no reason why the prosecutrix did not approach the authorities either on 31.08.2021 when she made a complaint to the SHO or 27.05.2022 when she registered the FIR.

For the said reasons, proceedings in the FIR 413/2022 u/s 323/427/506/509/354/354D/376(2)(n)
IPC and Sections 6 read with 5(1) of POCSO Act and in the alternative Section 376(2)(n) IPC pending before learned ASJ, South West District, Dwarka Courts titled 'State vs. Jai Kishore Kumar'
shall remain stayed till the next date of hearing.
JASMEET SINGH, J MAY 18, 2023/DM
